title: Mamata Banerjee's Party Is Fracturing. MLAs Are Revolting, Leaders Are in Jail, and Crowds Are Throwing Eggs.
excerpt: The Trinamool Congress is facing its worst internal crisis since coming to power in 2011. With over a dozen leaders behind bars, mass resignations in civic bodies, and public anger spilling into the streets, the party is scrambling to hold together ahead of the 2026 Bengal assembly election.
body:
The images from West Bengal this past week would have been unthinkable even a year ago. Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee — Mamata Banerjee's nephew and the party's presumed heir — was pelted with eggs by an angry mob in Sonarpur on May 30. He had to don a helmet to leave the area safely. In the days since, TMC functionaries across multiple districts have faced similar public fury, with egg attacks becoming a recurring form of protest against a party that has ruled Bengal since 2011.

The eggs are a symptom. The disease is deeper.

## The Revolt From Within

At least a dozen Trinamool Congress legislators have broken openly with the party leadership in recent weeks. Rebel MLA Ritabrata Banerjee — no relation to the chief minister — has given multiple television interviews accusing the party of abandoning its own workers during post-election violence and of prioritising loyalty to the family over governance. Other dissenters have echoed his complaints, pointing to what they describe as a culture of corruption and authoritarianism within the party machinery.

The internal crisis has been compounded by law enforcement. Over a dozen TMC leaders are currently behind bars on charges ranging from corruption to land-grabbing. Mass resignations have swept through civic bodies, with party functionaries at the municipal level abandoning ship ahead of what they see as an inevitable electoral reckoning.

"The TMC leadership has stayed indoors rather than supporting the cadre during post-poll violence," one rebel MLA told the media this week, capturing a sense of betrayal that has spread across party ranks.

## Mamata's Response: Restructure and Centralise

Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee has responded to the crisis with a sweeping party overhaul. Derek O'Brien and Dola Sen have been appointed as national joint secretaries. Chandrima Bhattacharya has been elevated to state president of the West Bengal Pradesh Trinamool Congress Committee, replacing the previous leadership team. New vice-presidents, general secretaries and executive members have been installed.

In a recent closed-door meeting with party legislators, Banerjee delivered a pointed warning. She cautioned MLAs against public statements that embarrass the party — a direct reference to veteran legislator Madan Mitra, who recently claimed that buying a seat on the party's district committee in exchange for money was "quite common." Mitra later wrote an apology letter, but the damage was done.

Banerjee also flagged internal factional fighting, specifically naming Malda and West Burdwan districts as trouble spots where rival TMC camps have been openly clashing.

## The Bengal 2026 Backdrop

The stakes could not be higher. West Bengal's assembly election is approaching, and the BJP has sharpened its attacks. The party has accused the TMC of failing farmers, enabling corruption through its infamous "cut-money" culture, and presiding over a state where infiltration across the Bangladesh border has gone unchecked.

Eggs thrown at Abhishek Banerjee represent more than spontaneous anger. They reflect a Bengali public that had given the TMC commanding mandates in 2011, 2016 and 2021 but is now openly questioning whether the party has earned another term.

The BJP's campaign is straightforward: fifteen years of corruption, violence, and unchecked power. The Congress and Left parties, historically strong in Bengal but marginalised over the past decade, scent opportunity in the TMC's disarray.

## What Mamata Does Next

On Monday, Banerjee and Abhishek Banerjee will travel to New Delhi for an INDIA bloc meeting, signalling that the national opposition alliance remains a priority even as the home front burns. Banerjee is also preparing to challenge developments around the Leader of Opposition position in court — a procedural battle that underscores how much ground the TMC has lost in legislative arithmetic.

The restructuring may stabilise the party apparatus in the short term. But the underlying problem is not structural — it is a crisis of trust between a party that has governed Bengal for fifteen years and a public that increasingly sees it as part of the problem rather than the solution.

Whether the egg-throwing crowds of Sonarpur represent a passing spasm of anger or the first cracks in a political edifice that took decades to build will become clear in the months ahead. For now, Mamata Banerjee faces the most serious internal challenge of her career — and the 2026 assembly election is closer than it appears.

**Sources:** Bhasha Times, The Hindu, India Tribune, News89
